answer: I'd like to talk about the day I found out I had got my current job, because it was a real turning point for me. A moment of wonderful news that I will never forget was when I found out I had been accepted for a position I had desperately wanted. It was a role at an education consultancy, helping students apply to study abroad, which suited both my BBA and my own interest in international education. I had applied weeks earlier and had almost given up hope, so the email from the director caught me completely [[off guard]]. I was actually sitting at a tea stall with a friend when my phone buzzed, and I assumed it was another rejection. I remember reading it several times, hardly able to believe it, feeling utterly [[elated]]. My first instinct was to call my family, who had supported me throughout the stressful application process. My mother answered, and I could hear her telling my father and sister in the background before I had even finished. Their reaction was just as [[overjoyed]] as mine, which made the moment even sweeter. What made the news so meaningful was how hard I had worked and how uncertain the outcome had felt. The relief was almost as strong as the happiness; it was genuinely [[euphoric]]. That evening we celebrated together over my mother's cooking, and I felt an immense sense of [[accomplishment]]. Honestly, it remains one of the happiest days of my life, and it reminded me that persistence really can pay off.

followUps.q: Who is usually the first person you share good news with?
followUps.answer: Usually my mother, because she worries about me the most, so good news means a lot to her. My younger sister is a close second, since she tends to find out everything anyway.

followUps.q: Do you prefer to receive news by phone or in person?
followUps.answer: In person, if possible. You can see someone's face and share the moment properly. That said, for something like a job offer, an email is fine, because you can read it again and again.

note: Made the news his consultancy job offer; added who sent it and where he was; family celebrated at home since he lives with them.
